what: The side panel shows the title, State, Assignee, Priority, QC, Sprint, Due, created/updated dates, Reporter, Description, Links, Mentioned on Telegram and Comments.

how.t: Click "Tickets"
Click a ticket row (click the title) to open the side panel

how: See State, Assignee, Priority, QC, Sprint, Due, Description, Links, Mentioned on Telegram, Comments; click a ticket under "Links" to switch to it

how.t: Click the ID at the top of the side panel to open it on YouTrack
Click ✕ "Close" (or Esc)

keys: ticket details description comments links mentioned on telegram tags

title: UI flow: the ticket's screens and the taps between them
what: The AI reads the ticket's AC, rules and Zeplin links (for a sub-task, its parent story in full, where the ACs, the "Luồng màn" tree and the Zeplin links live) and builds the flow: which screens exist, which button leads where, which popups show, where Back goes. Screens with a Zeplin link are drawn from the real design image, each button a tap area in its place on it (matched by the text on the button; buttons not found on the design show as rows below); needs the Zeplin MCP set up. View it as a map or tap through it like a prototype, fix it up, then press Update to write uiflow-<ticket>.html onto the ticket with a comment listing what changed. The uiflow-<ticket>.html row under Attachments opens this same view. If someone else has just updated it, the app says so and offers the new version instead of overwriting it.

how.t: Click "Tickets"
Click a ticket row (click the title) to open the side panel
Click "UI flow"

how: No file yet: pick "Screens only" (code builds the Zeplin screens and buttons, no links, 0 tokens, a few seconds) or "Screens + links" (the AI reads the AC to draw the taps), then press the button below the cards. Pick the platform (Mobile / Web, with how many screens each size has) right below the cards; it applies to both ways: the other platform's screens are not built; once there is a flow, pick it in the "Render again" question. Under the title the panel shows how many Zeplin screens the ticket has, how many flow lines are unclear (to fix in the ticket), and the most tokens and estimated cost of an AI render; with no Zeplin link, "Screens only" is locked. The estimated tokens show beside the button; add a note for the AI if needed, then press "Render bằng AI" (or "Dựng màn"); while it runs you can press "Dừng render"

While it renders, the view shows its progress: % done, how long it has run and roughly how long is left, each stage (reading the ticket and story, each Zeplin screen, the AI planning the flow, each screen drawn, each button linked to its screen, the check) with its numbers and time, the screens just drawn and the links just made

Closing the view mid-render does not stop the AI: the "UI flow" button shows a dot while it runs; open it again to follow its progress or get the result. When a render shows an error (a lost connection too), the AI run has stopped and the line names the stage it failed at: click "Render with AI" to run it again

A button Zeplin has no text layer for (a list flattened into the image): with "Screens + links" the AI looks at the design image to place its tap area (one more short AI run); that area can be edited like a hand-drawn one and is kept on a re-render. A button the AI cannot find gets a warning: draw its tap area by hand.

While it draws, each step has a tag: "AI" (highlighted) means the AI reads / writes and spends AI tokens; "Code" means the dashboard handles it itself (reading the ticket, reading Zeplin, checking the result), no tokens

Once rendered, the bar below says how many screens and links the AI drew and how long it took; on "Update" it shows the Zeplin images being embedded (n/total), then the file being uploaded to the ticket
With a flow: use the toolbar inside the frame (Map / Prototype, Edit, the screen finder, Fit, Check)

"Check" has two tabs. "To review": gaps in the flow, buttons not found on the design image, screens with no Zeplin link, bad data; filter by kind with the count buttons; while editing, a row opens that screen / button to fix. The "To add" kind: steps / screens / popups the ticket mentions that have no design yet. The AI does not draw them (the map only holds screens with a Zeplin image); it lists them here with where they are reached from, the condition and the AC. While editing, click a row to paste that step's Zeplin link: the screen is added with the right kind, linked from where it is reached, and the row leaves the list (one Undo step); ✕ drops a step that will never get a screen. A ticket with no Zeplin link at all is still drawn from its description, as before. The "Unclear" kind: warnings from the render that just ran (e.g. some branches in the ticket are not clear enough, a story could not be read); shown until the flow is saved to the ticket. Outside Edit mode, click an AC chip on a screen (e.g. "AC3.5") to light only the screens and arrows that carry that AC code; click the chip again or press Esc to clear. "Test checklist": the code lists tap paths from the start screen that cross every link, with their conditions, and the links it cannot reach; "Copy" to paste into test cases or the ticket's AI.

Select a screen while editing: the properties panel opens bottom-left; its header has the kind + name, a ▶ button ("▶ Start screen"), a bin ("Delete") and ✕ ("Deselect", or Esc). Press ▶ so the prototype, the map and the checklist start there (press again to go back to the first screen). With Edit on, a tool group appears next to the Edit button: "+ From Zeplin" (the one way to add a screen by hand) and 3 icons "Re-arrange", "↶ Undo", "↷ Redo" (hover for the name; ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z); a run of arrow-key moves counts as one step.

Click a screen on the map, then "Prototype": Prototype goes on from that screen. No screen picked: the first time it starts at the start screen, later it returns to where you were. Change the start screen on the map (the ▶ button while editing) and the next visit to Prototype begins again at the new start screen. A screen just added with "+ From Zeplin" is placed in free space (right of the last screen when the middle of the view is taken), never on top of another, and does not move where Prototype stands.

No start screen set: the flow check lists "No start screen" and Prototype's bottom bar says "No start screen set" (meanwhile Prototype and the checklist start at the first screen). In Prototype, press "▶ Start screen" on the bottom bar to make the screen shown the start screen, press again to unset; no edit mode needed. Press "Update" to save it.
In Prototype, tap an empty spot on the screen image: every tap area of that screen lights up for a moment.

To view the flow you are editing outside the app (an unsaved draft included): press the "Download the HTML file" icon in the header; the file opens offline and nothing is written to the ticket. The bar below shows the image-embedding progress; when done a line says the file is ready, with a "Download" button in case the browser did not save it by itself. If the ticket changed after the flow was last updated, the view says so; "Render again with AI" keeps the notes, hand-drawn tap areas, start screen (and positions, when no screen is new) of matching screens.
The "Find a screen" box: type a screen name (accents optional), a Zeplin link or an id; matches get a yellow outline, Up/Down picks one, Enter goes to it, Esc clears. Finding never changes the flow.

Click "Edit": "+ From Zeplin" takes a Zeplin screen link and adds the screen with its name and design image (a link already in the flow jumps to that screen; a Zeplin error offers "Retry" or "Add it without the image"); "Re-arrange" lays every screen out again, ⌘Z takes it back. Select a screen: the properties panel only has the screen kind, the Zeplin link, its "Note" (plain text, a ✎ mark on the screen, Esc cancels, kept in the flow only, never posted as a ticket comment), or "+ Tap area" and drag on the image to draw a button (or press Enter for one mid-screen). Keyboard only: find a screen and press Enter to select it; its tap areas are in the "Tap areas" row of the properties panel (hover a name to see it on the map; a screen with no design image has a "Buttons" row with "+ Button" instead). Select a tap area / button: it is filled with a bright ring, the screen's other areas dim and only its own arrows stay lit; the ‹ button in the panel header goes back to its screen (an arrow has ‹ back to its source screen too). On the image: drag to move it, drag its corner to resize, edit the Area (px) numbers, "Redraw area" or "Match by text". Move a screen by dragging its title bar or with the arrow keys (Shift: bigger steps); arrow keys also move the selected area. Select a screen, button or arrow: only it and the screens / arrows linked to it stay bright, the rest dims; Esc clears the selection. Zoomed out, arrow labels and the title bar over a design image are hidden to keep the map clean (zoom in, hover the screen or select it to see them); link dots only show on the screen under the pointer or selected.

After an edit the bar below says there are unsaved changes. No file on the ticket yet (the flow is only a draft): the bar has the draft status, "Discard draft" and "Save to ticket" for the first write. Editing a flow that already has a file: the bar only has "Update"; the draft line only shows when saving the draft failed, with "Retry". Press ✕ at the end of the bar to hide it (the draft is kept; the small line below has "Update the ticket" to bring it back).

how.t: The ↻ button (only once there is a flow): "Render again with AI". The ← button on the left closes UI flow. The download icon: "Download the HTML file" (the flow on screen, an unsaved draft included). The bin icon: "Delete UI flow" (removes the file from the ticket after asking; unsaved: "Discard render")

how: There is no token limit and nothing is cut any more: a risky render (many tokens, many screens, unclear flow) shows a warning with the tokens per source; press "Xem dòng" on the unclear-flow warning to see each line the code could not draw and why (screen name not matching a Zeplin link title, matching several screens, wrong format); fix it in the ticket as `Màn A -- "Nút" --> Màn B` so the code draws it and the AI need not guess. Each line has a #number: untick it so the AI does not draw that link, press #number or the whole row to put the line in the AI box; "Tick all / Untick all" at the top of each group switches the whole group; links in a line open in the browser. UI flow defaults to "Chỉ màn hình" (0 tokens). With "Màn + liên kết", render always opens the pre-check first: it counts tokens when it opens (with a waiting scene), and holds the model / effort at the bottom of the box, beside Cancel and Render; the platform picked before is named there. The "Split into n parts" card shows the tokens of all parts together (each part sends the ticket again). Zeplin screens of the other platform (web / desktop size when drawing mobile, mobile size when drawing web) are not sent and not shown in the box: the token and screen counts and the warnings (flow lines linking to those screens included) cover only the chosen platform. A line naming a screen has a button to open it in Zeplin. The "Hỏi AI" panel on the right of the warning is for questions, links or more flow description; its answers and the unticked lines go with the render on "Render kèm phần đã làm rõ"; press "Phân tích bằng AI" for a light model to say why and what to do (it reads the numbers only, never the ticket), the "Build screens" card for a 0-token version, or "Render bằng AI" for the AI to read the whole ticket. It only refuses an input past every model's context. Beside the tokens is an estimated price (~$) from recent runs on that same model. "Render lại bằng AI" defaults to "Chỉ vẽ phần mới": the current links stay and the AI only adds what is new, for far fewer tokens; untick it to redraw everything. The per-path test checklist is already in the diagram. A ticket with more than 12 screens gets "Chia {n} phần" in the warning: parts of 12 screens, each with the full AC, run 3 at a time and joined into one diagram (faster, fewer errors on a light model, more input tokens in total); if one part fails the whole render fails so it can be retried. Esc only cancels what you are doing in the diagram (drops the selection, stops drawing a frame, closes an open form); only the ✕ button closes UI flow. If the Zeplin design changed after the last Update (size or texts on a screen), the bottom bar names those screens with an "Cập nhật" button to embed the new images in the file; for new screens / buttons use "Render lại bằng AI" with "Chỉ vẽ phần mới". Only files saved from this version on can be compared. Prototype: a screen opened from several screens (A → C, B → C) has a back link to each; "Quay lại" returns to the one that opened it on the path walked.
keys: ui flow uiflow screens tap flow prototype zeplin render ai update file on ticket find screen note from zeplin re-arrange tap area to review test checklist start screen redo review changes

title: Ask again in the group from a ticket
what: Under each Telegram message mentioning the ticket there is an "Ask in the group" link: it opens that group's Q&A with the new question box prefilled "About <ID> <title>: ". Add the @name of the person to ask, then Post so the question gets a #QA code and is tracked.
how: Open a ticket and look at the "Mentioned on Telegram" section
Click "Ask in the group", finish the question with an @name, then Post
keys: ask again in group qa telegram ticket tag ask someone

title: Follow up when a ticket moves to Fixed / Done (even while on Telegram)
what: When one of your tickets that someone asked about on Telegram moves to Fixed / Done, the app reminds you to get back to the person who asked. The server checks every 3 minutes even with no page open (the same round wakes tags snoozed until a ticket is done); the list is kept on this machine, so every browser sees the same one. Reply to that message (on the web or your phone) and the item is done; click X to skip it.
how: A notice at the bottom of the screen shows "<ID>: …"
Open the message in To do to write your follow-up
keys: follow up fixed done notification asker telegram ticket

title: Previous / next ticket
what: Step through the tickets of the list you came from without closing the side panel.

how.t: Click "Tickets"
Click a ticket row (click the title) to open the side panel
Click › "Next ticket" (key j)
Click ‹ "Previous ticket" (key k)

how: The "n/N" number next to it shows the position in the list
keys: previous ticket next ticket next previous j k switch ticket

title: Change State / Priority / Assignee
what: Changes the ticket's State, Priority and Assignee directly on YouTrack (State follows the workflow); the notice has an undo button. For a ticket from another project, the Assignee / QC list is that project's team.

how.t: Click "Tickets"
Click a ticket row (click the title) to open the side panel
Click State (with the ▾ arrow) and pick a new value
Click Priority and pick a new value
Under Assignee, pick a new person or "Unassigned"

how: Click undo in the notice if it was a mistake
keys: change state change priority change assignee workflow undo

title: Post a comment to YouTrack
what: Write and post a comment on the ticket right from the dashboard. Type @ to mention a project member (inserts @login, YouTrack notifies them).

how.t: Click "Tickets"
Click a ticket row (click the title) to open the side panel
Scroll down and type in the "New comment" box (type @ and a few letters of a name to mention someone)
Click "Send comment"

title: Tag YouTrack members with @
what: Type @ in a ticket's comment box or in the description box when creating a ticket to open the member list (the project's team), keep typing to filter by name or login. Picking a person inserts @login; YouTrack notifies the person mentioned.
how: Type @ and a few letters of the name in the "New comment" box or the description box (Create ticket › Manual)
↑ ↓ to choose, Enter or Tab to insert, Esc to close the list
keys: tag tag name @ members login youtrack comment description create ticket

title: Similar / related tickets + AI duplicate check
what: Lists tickets with similar titles (with a % match); the AI can judge which are duplicates and which are only related, and suggest merging/linking/keeping them apart.

how.t: Click "Tickets"
Click a ticket row (click the title) to open the side panel

how: Scroll to the "Similar / related tickets" section (only when there are similar titles); click a row to open that ticket

how.t: Click "AI duplicate check"

keys: similar tickets related duplicate ai duplicate check
